stem: A Massachusetts company holds a wholesale druggist controlled substance registration and is opening a second distribution warehouse in another city. Its counsel says the existing registration covers the new site and runs on the same two-year cycle as the group's pharmacy registrations. What is the position?

choices.text: Counsel is right on both points, since one registrant holds one registration.
Counsel is right on coverage but wrong on the cycle, which is three years.
Counsel is wrong on coverage but right that a two-year cycle applies.
Counsel is wrong on both: a separate registration is needed and the term is one year.
Counsel is wrong on coverage, and the wholesale registration has no fixed expiry.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 11.05 requires a SEPARATE controlled substance registration at each principal place of business where the registrant manufactures, distributes or dispenses. 247 CMR 11.06 sets terms by registrant type: two years from January 1st of each even-numbered year for a pharmacy and for an outsourcing facility, but ONE year from DECEMBER 1st of each year for a wholesale druggist.

choice_analysis.A: Registration attaches to each principal place of business.
choice_analysis.B: Coverage is wrong and no three-year cycle exists.
choice_analysis.C: The two-year cycle belongs to pharmacies and outsourcing facilities.
choice_analysis.E: The wholesale registration has a stated annual expiry.

related_facts: The pharmacy and outsourcing facility cycles both begin in even-numbered years
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates assume a single registrant holds a single registration on a single cycle.

reasoning_steps: Apply the separate-registration rule to the second warehouse
Read the term stated for that type
